name: Build the muzzle flash effect prefab
instruction: Create a layered muzzle flash prefab: edit scenes/effects/muzzle_flash_effect.tscn so the root Node3D uses scripts/generic_effect_handler.gd, targets its Optional Light export at an OmniLight child named MuzzleFlash, and keeps a 0.2 second fade. Add SmokeParticles configured with zero gravity and a StandardMaterial3D mesh using a radial GradientTexture2D. Simulate a volumetric smoke puff via using particle billboard mode for billboarding, plus a pair of opposing GPUParticles3D named MuzzleFireLeft and MuzzleFireRight that emit one-shot bursts. Each muzzle fire particle system must rely on the provided assets/shaders/muzzle_flash.gdshader ShaderMaterial and include a draw-pass QuadMesh so the burst renders from both sides. Wire the scene into scenes/main.tscn so Main instantiates the finished effect.

metadata.tutorial_source: YouTube: Bonkahe - Godot 3D - Making a FPS Horror Game (C#) | 03 | Gun Mechanics
metadata.transcript_excerpt: the muzzle flash has a light but if we go ahead and turn that off it also has several particle effects that are all children of it … we also have a custom Shader … we're going to go ahead and create a kind of generic effect Handler … if the optional light is not null we tween the light energy back down to zero
